detail: Direct, smart and full policy paths were distinguished by actual LAN egress and proxy observations.
Original source, owned marks, MSS and the FastTrack exception were verified with an unaffected peer.
The affected connection changed path and the independent connection survived.
After the selected server stopped, the LAN client reached the other proxy egress.
Native and steered DNS traffic reached the expected resolvers over TCP and UDP.
The proxied client encountered the IPv6 guard and the direct client retained external IPv6 connectivity.
Real QUIC Initial packets distinguished name-based routing at the same destination address.
The service repaired owned drift. The WAN-side witness saw no closed-client leak during route loss.
Two owner commands restored ordinary routing with both containers stopped. Service recovery restored steering and protection.
